claims.title: Ammon, Moab and Edom emerge
claims.summary: As the Iron Age began, three settled kingdoms took shape on the plateau east of the Jordan, each with its own capital, language and national god, controlling the caravan trade of the King's Highway.

sources.label: Jordan: A Country Study
sources.publisher: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.title: Ammon regains its independence
claims.summary: According to the biblical account, the kingdom of Ammon, centred on Rabbath Ammon (modern Amman), reasserted its independence after the death of the Israelite king David.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Jordan: From the Iron Age kingdoms east of the Jordan and the rose-red city of Petra to the Hashemite kingdom of Amman.", terralore.co/country/JOR/chronicle#ev-960bce-ammon-regains-its-independence, claim TL:JOR:event:960bce:ammon-regains-its-independence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Mesha Stele of Moab
claims.summary: King Mesha of Moab erected a stone inscription recording his wars and building works, one of the earliest royal inscriptions from the lands east of the Jordan.

sources.label: Jordan: A Country Study
sources.publisher: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.title: Alexander the Great and the end of Persian rule
claims.summary: The conquests of Alexander brought the region into the Hellenistic world, hastening the eclipse of the old Iron Age kingdoms and opening the way to Greek and later Roman cities.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Jordan: From the Iron Age kingdoms east of the Jordan and the rose-red city of Petra to the Hashemite kingdom of Amman.", terralore.co/country/JOR/chronicle#ev-332bce-alexander-the-great-and-the-end-of-persian-rule, claim TL:JOR:event:332bce:alexander-the-great-and-the-end-of-persian-rule, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Nabataeans resist the Greeks at Petra
claims.summary: The Nabataean Arabs, established around Petra, repelled campaigns by the Hellenistic successors of Alexander, marking their emergence as a distinct desert power controlling the caravan trade.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Jordan: From the Iron Age kingdoms east of the Jordan and the rose-red city of Petra to the Hashemite kingdom of Amman.", terralore.co/country/JOR/chronicle#ev-312bce-the-nabataeans-resist-the-greeks-at-petra, claim TL:JOR:event:312bce:the-nabataeans-resist-the-greeks-at-petra, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Petra reaches its golden age
claims.summary: At the height of the incense trade the Nabataeans carved Petra's monumental tomb-temples and engineered an elaborate system of dams, channels and cisterns to sustain a great city in the desert.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Jordan: From the Iron Age kingdoms east of the Jordan and the rose-red city of Petra to the Hashemite kingdom of Amman.", terralore.co/country/JOR/chronicle#ev-100bce-petra-reaches-its-golden-age, claim TL:JOR:event:100bce:petra-reaches-its-golden-age, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rome annexes the Nabataean kingdom
claims.summary: The emperor Trajan absorbed the Nabataean realm as the province of Arabia Petraea, ending Nabataean independence as Roman power extended across the region.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Jordan: From the Iron Age kingdoms east of the Jordan and the rose-red city of Petra to the Hashemite kingdom of Amman.", terralore.co/country/JOR/chronicle#ev-106-rome-annexes-the-nabataean-kingdom, claim TL:JOR:event:106:rome-annexes-the-nabataean-kingdom, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Petra inscribed as a World Heritage Site
claims.summary: UNESCO inscribed Petra on the World Heritage List as a unique artistic achievement and an outstanding architectural ensemble of the early centuries BCE and CE.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Jordan: From the Iron Age kingdoms east of the Jordan and the rose-red city of Petra to the Hashemite kingdom of Amman.", terralore.co/country/JOR/chronicle#ev-1985-petra-inscribed-as-a-world-heritage-site, claim TL:JOR:event:1985:petra-inscribed-as-a-world-heritage-site, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Pompey creates the Decapolis
claims.summary: Rome's reorganisation of the East grouped Gerasa (Jerash) and neighbouring Greek-style cities into the Decapolis, a league of self-governing towns that prospered under Roman rule.

claims.title: Jerash flourishes as a Roman city
claims.summary: Gerasa was rebuilt with colonnaded streets, an oval forum, temples and theatres, becoming one of the wealthiest cities of the Roman Near East and leaving ruins still visible today.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Jordan: From the Iron Age kingdoms east of the Jordan and the rose-red city of Petra to the Hashemite kingdom of Amman.", terralore.co/country/JOR/chronicle#ev-100-jerash-flourishes-as-a-roman-city, claim TL:JOR:event:100:jerash-flourishes-as-a-roman-city, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Christian Byzantium and the mosaics of Um er-Rasas
claims.summary: Under Byzantine rule Christianity spread across the plateau and church floors were laid with elaborate mosaics, preserved most fully at Um er-Rasas, later a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Jordan: From the Iron Age kingdoms east of the Jordan and the rose-red city of Petra to the Hashemite kingdom of Amman.", terralore.co/country/JOR/chronicle#ev-451-christian-byzantium-and-the-mosaics-of-um-er, claim TL:JOR:event:451:christian-byzantium-and-the-mosaics-of-um-er, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Battle of the Yarmuk
claims.summary: Muslim Arab armies decisively defeated the Byzantines near the Yarmuk River, ending Roman rule over the region and bringing the lands east of the Jordan into the new Islamic world.

sources.label: Jordan: A Country Study
sources.publisher: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.title: Umayyad rule and the desert castles
claims.summary: Governing from Damascus, the Umayyad caliphs built fortified desert residences across the eastern plateau, including Quseir Amra with its celebrated frescoes of early Islamic secular art.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Jordan: From the Iron Age kingdoms east of the Jordan and the rose-red city of Petra to the Hashemite kingdom of Amman.", terralore.co/country/JOR/chronicle#ev-661-umayyad-rule-and-the-desert-castles, claim TL:JOR:event:661:umayyad-rule-and-the-desert-castles, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Quseir Amra is built
claims.summary: An Umayyad prince raised the bath-house and pleasure palace of Quseir Amra, whose figurative murals make it one of the most important survivals of early Islamic art; UNESCO inscribed it in 1985.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Jordan: From the Iron Age kingdoms east of the Jordan and the rose-red city of Petra to the Hashemite kingdom of Amman.", terralore.co/country/JOR/chronicle#ev-723-quseir-amra-is-built, claim TL:JOR:event:723:quseir-amra-is-built, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Ottomans conquer the region
claims.summary: After defeating the Mamluks, the Ottoman Turks absorbed the lands east of the Jordan into their empire as part of the province of Syria, ruling for four centuries.

sources.publisher: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.title: The Hejaz Railway crosses the plateau
claims.summary: The Ottomans completed the Hejaz Railway through the territory, linking Damascus toward the holy cities and binding the region more tightly to the empire on the eve of the Arab Revolt.

claims.title: The Great Arab Revolt begins
claims.summary: Sharif Hussein of Mecca, supported by Britain, launched the Arab Revolt against the Ottoman Empire; his sons Faisal and Abdullah led its forces toward Syria, aided by T. E. Lawrence.

claims.summary: After the Cairo Conference, Abdullah ibn Hussein formed a government east of the Jordan under British mandate, establishing Hashemite rule and the Emirate of Transjordan.

claims.title: Independence of the Hashemite Kingdom
claims.summary: Following the Treaty of London, the British mandate ended and Transjordan became a fully independent kingdom, with Abdullah re-designated as king; 25 May is celebrated as Independence Day.

claims.summary: After his Arab Legion occupied the West Bank and East Jerusalem in the 1948 war, King Abdullah formally annexed the territory and renamed the enlarged state the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan.

claims.summary: Abdullah I was shot dead on the steps of the al-Aqsa Mosque in Jerusalem by a Palestinian gunman, opening a brief succession crisis before his grandson Hussein came to the throne.

claims.summary: After his father Talal was declared unfit to rule, the young Hussein bin Talal took full constitutional powers, beginning a reign of nearly half a century that shaped the modern kingdom.

claims.summary: In the war with Israel, Jordan lost the West Bank and East Jerusalem, and a fresh wave of Palestinian refugees fled into the East Bank, deepening the kingdom's demographic transformation.

claims.title: Black September
claims.summary: King Hussein's army moved against armed Palestinian factions that had built a state within the state; after intense fighting and a brief Syrian incursion, the guerrillas were expelled by July 1971.

claims.summary: King Hussein signed the Wadi Araba treaty with Israel, ending the state of war and making Jordan the second Arab country, after Egypt, to conclude a formal peace with Israel.

claims.summary: On the death of King Hussein, his son Abdullah II ascended the throne, going on to promote economic reform while steering Jordan through war in Iraq, the Arab Spring and a vast refugee influx.
